device_description: A portable, single-patient negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) system delivering continuous and intermittent sub-atmospheric pressure (-40 to -200 mmHg) to a sealed wound dressing via a battery-powered pump, intended for management of acute and chronic wounds.
intended_purpose: Promotion of wound healing through the application of controlled negative pressure to chronic, acute, traumatic, dehisced, and surgically closed wounds, and to skin grafts and flaps, in adult patients.
inclusion_criteria: Human clinical studies (RCT, cohort, case series with >=10 patients)
Reports clinical outcomes, performance, or safety of NPWT in target indications
exclusion_criteria: Animal or in vitro studies only
Editorials, letters, conference abstracts without data
Full text not available in English
track1_inclusion_criteria: Human clinical study of NPWT or a named equivalent/comparator device (RCT, controlled/cohort study, prospective or retrospective series with >=10 patients, or a systematic review / meta-analysis that pools such studies)
Reports clinical performance, effectiveness, or safety outcomes of NPWT in an indication within the device's intended purpose
Published within the protocol date range
track1_exclusion_criteria: Animal or in vitro studies only
Narrative/non-systematic reviews, editorials, letters, or conference abstracts that report no primary or pooled outcome data
Indication outside the device's intended purpose
NPWT mentioned only incidentally and not reported as a study endpoint
Individual case reports or series with fewer than 10 patients
Full text not available in English
track2_inclusion_criteria: Characterises the standard of care, the available therapeutic/management/diagnostic ALTERNATIVES, or benchmark clinical outcomes for the relevant medical condition(s) (MEDDEV 2.7/1 rev 4, Appendix A4)
Clinical practice guidelines, consensus or position statements from professional medical associations ARE eligible
Systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and health technology assessment (HTA) reviews on the management of the condition(s) ARE eligible
Applicable standards and guidance documents on the condition or its treatment ARE eligible
Primary clinical studies that define current treatment outcomes or alternatives for the condition are also eligible
Published within the protocol date range; English language
track2_exclusion_criteria: Not about the relevant medical condition(s) or therapeutic area

Addresses only a contributing or background factor (e.g. nutrition, general epidemiology, cost/economic burden, basic pathophysiology) WITHOUT characterising the standard of care, treatment, or management options
Animal or in vitro studies only
Individual case reports or very small series with no generalisable contribution to the state of the art
Bench/materials-science or device-engineering papers with no clinical relevance to standard of care
Full text not available in English

equivalent_devices.name: VacuHeal Pro NPWT System
equivalent_devices.regulatory_status: CE-marked under MDR 2017/745 (fictional, for demo). Certificate valid; based on an updated clinical evaluation.
equivalent_devices.relationship: Other manufacturer, same device group (portable single-patient NPWT). Not a predecessor/successor of the device under evaluation.
equivalent_devices.technical_characteristics: Similar design: battery-powered portable pump delivering controlled sub-atmospheric pressure via a sealed foam/film dressing. Pressure range -40 to -200 mmHg, continuous and intermittent modes, matching the device under evaluation. Same principle of operation (negative pressure applied to a sealed wound bed) and comparable critical performance (pressure accuracy +/- 10 mmHg, canister-based exudate management). Deployment method (adhesive drape + tubing + canister) is equivalent. PRRC to confirm software/control algorithm comparability against VacuHeal technical file.
equivalent_devices.biological_characteristics: Patient-contacting materials (polyurethane foam dressing, acrylic adhesive drape, silicone-bordered interface) are of the same families and contact the same tissues (wound bed, peri-wound intact skin) for comparable durations. Biocompatibility assessed per ISO 10993-1. PRRC attests material equivalence pending review of VacuHeal material specifications; any difference in foam pore size to be evaluated for clinical significance.
equivalent_devices.clinical_characteristics: Same clinical condition and indications (chronic, acute, traumatic, dehisced, surgically closed wounds; grafts and flaps), same intended purpose (promotion of wound healing via controlled negative pressure), same body sites, and same adult patient population. No clinically significant difference in expected clinical effect anticipated.
equivalent_devices.differences_and_justification: Identified differences: (1) VacuHeal foam pore size specified at 400-600 micron vs device-under-evaluation 450-650 micron; (2) VacuHeal default intermittent cycle 5 min on / 2 min off vs 3 min on / 2 min off. PRRC justification: both pore ranges fall within the established therapeutic window for granulation tissue formation reported in the literature, and intermittent cycle timing is clinician-adjustable on both devices; therefore neither difference is expected to trigger a clinically significant difference in safety or performance. (PRRC rationale - to be confirmed against full technical comparison; Vigil does not assess this.)
equivalent_devices.technical_documentation_access: Manufacturer has NO contractual access to VacuHeal's full technical documentation (different manufacturer). Equivalence rests on publicly available IFU, published literature, and the CE-marked status of VacuHeal. PRRC NOTE: per MDCG 2020-5, for a Class IIb non-implantable device a contract is not strictly required, but the manufacturer must demonstrate SUFFICIENT access to the data needed to substantiate the three characteristics. The PRRC must judge whether public-domain data is sufficient here, or whether equivalence cannot be claimed. THIS IS A PRRC DETERMINATION - Vigil only records the access level stated.

manufacturer_claims.claim: The device promotes healing of chronic wounds (diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, venous leg ulcers).
manufacturer_claims.acceptance_criterion: Published clinical evidence demonstrates wound closure / healing rates with NPWT at least comparable to standard-of-care moist wound dressings in the target indications.

manufacturer_claims.claim: The device prepares the wound bed for skin grafting.
manufacturer_claims.acceptance_criterion: Evidence shows improved granulation tissue formation and graft take rates with NPWT versus conventional dressings prior to grafting.

manufacturer_claims.claim: The device has an acceptable safety profile in adult wound-care patients.
manufacturer_claims.acceptance_criterion: Reported adverse events (bleeding, infection, pain, maceration) are within the range established for NPWT in the state-of-the-art literature, with no new or unexpected hazards.

pico_population: Adult patients with chronic, acute, traumatic, dehisced, or surgically closed wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, pressure ulcers, and venous leg ulcers; and patients requiring wound-bed preparation for skin grafts or flaps.
pico_intervention: Negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT) delivering controlled sub-atmospheric pressure (-40 to -200 mmHg) via a sealed wound dressing.
pico_comparator: Standard-of-care moist wound dressings (e.g. alginate, foam, hydrocolloid); wet-to-dry dressings; other NPWT systems.
pico_outcomes: Complete wound closure rate; time to healing; granulation tissue formation; wound area reduction; skin graft take rate; adverse events (infection, bleeding, pain, maceration); amputation rate (in diabetic foot ulcers).

alternative_treatments_strategy: Identify and assess alternative wound-management modalities (advanced dressings, conventional NPWT comparators, standard of care) via the Track 2 state-of-the-art search and clinical practice guidelines, to benchmark the device against current treatment options. [PRRC to finalise.]
pms_data_collection_strategy: Systematically collect and summarise PMS data (complaints, vigilance, PMCF where applicable) on the device and named equivalent via the Vigil PMS Monitor handoff; CER-relevant signals are surfaced for PRRC triage and feed the CER update cycle. [PRRC to confirm methodology and frequency.]
next_evaluation_justification: As a well-established technology (stable, mature NPWT design with a long market history and no significant safety signals), a 24-month clinical evaluation update interval is proposed, supported by continuous PMS monitoring that would trigger an earlier update on any emerging signal. [PRRC to confirm against risk class and current PMS trend data.]
